# `obliquity()` {#fn-obliquity}

A05 checked the January true obliquity at modern and prehistoric test epochs against direct engine values. [A05 results](a05-solar-limits.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-obliquity)

```{=html}
<p>The tilt changes over archaeological timescales. For each supplied astronomical year the
calculation uses Gregorian 1 January at noon UT, requests the obliquity/nutation record
from Swiss Ephemeris and returns its first element, the true obliquity in degrees. An
annual value is a reference for limiting declinations rather than a search for the
instant of solstice.
</p>
```

<details><summary>Method references</summary>

```{=html}
<p>Laskar, J. et al. (2004), A long-term numerical
solution for the insolation quantities of the Earth, <em>Astron.
Astroph.</em>, 428, 261-285, doi:10.1051/0004-6361:20041335.
</p>



```

</details>

**Interpretation and limits.** Separate the annual obliquity reference from the approximate local parallax correction. A limiting declination used as a target has a different meaning from a position calculated for an observed instant.


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>year</code></th><td><code>skyscapeR.env$cur.year</code></td><td><p>Year for which to calculate the obliquity. Historical labels such as <code>"3700 BC"</code> are accepted by <code>astroYear</code>.
Defaults to present year as given by <em>Sys.Date</em></p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>Numeric obliquity of the ecliptic in degrees, one value per astronomical year.
</p>
```

</details>

**Implementation.** `R/mechanics.R`.
